metadata.title: Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
metadata.abstract: We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. In the case where the ambient metric evolves by a self-similar solution to the Ricci-Bourguignon flow, we characterize the associated mean curvature solitons and derive a Huisken monotonicity-type formula adapted to the Ricci-Bourguignon setting. As a consequence, we show that, in compact ambient manifolds, type-I singularities of the mean curvature flow in a gradient shrinking Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background have, after suitable parabolic rescaling, weighted minimal hypersurfaces as their limiting models, while in the noncompact setting, we establish the corresponding result for a gradient shrinking Schouten soliton background. This provides a geometric framework for understanding how the ambient scalar curvature influences the formation and structure of singularity models for the mean curvature flow. We also show how to construct explicit examples of mean curvature flow in a gradient Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background.
